domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Establish subtraction-ready representation
skills.definition: Prepare quantities so subtraction can proceed by rewriting numbers into compatible forms, including finding a common denominator for fractional parts and normalizing whole or mixed numbers into subtraction-ready form.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory setup skills that occur before core subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making the operands compatible for subtraction. They are distinct at fine grain, but at K=5 they can be merged without losing the major diagnostic distinction between setup, subtraction, regrouping, and finishing.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole-number parts of mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because this is the core execution step and has strong independent diagnostic value. Students may prepare correctly yet still make arithmetic or alignment errors here.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole-number part when direct subtraction of fractional parts would produce a negative result.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because borrowing/regrouping produces a distinctive error pattern and does not occur in all items. It remains diagnostically important to distinguish from ordinary subtraction.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or eliminate a zero fractional part after subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a post-subtraction operation with its own common error patterns, such as failing to reduce or mishandling zero fractional parts.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Express the completed result in an appropriate final form, such as a mixed number, fraction, or integer, by combining whole and fractional parts when needed.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final presentation is conceptually different from simplification: a student may compute and simplify correctly but still fail to express the answer in the proper form.
